title: Data Analyst
story: Bazaarline is an online store selling kitchen, home, personal-care and electronics products across India. You are the analyst the category and growth teams come to with questions.

tables.name: customers
tables.about: One row per customer: city, state, segment, signup date.

tables.name: products
tables.about: Catalogue: category, brand, cost price and list price (INR).

tables.name: orders
tables.about: One row per order in 2024: date, channel, status, payment method.

tables.name: order_items
tables.about: Lines of each order. Line revenue = quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount).

tasks.title: Orders by status
tasks.question: How many orders are there in each status? Return status and orders.
tasks.solution: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY status
tasks.hint: GROUP BY the status column and COUNT(*).
tasks.starter:
-- Orders by status
SELECT *
FROM orders
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Top cities by customers
tasks.question: List the 5 cities with the most customers. Return city and customers, highest first; break ties by city name A to Z.
tasks.solution: SELECT city, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customers GROUP BY city ORDER BY customers DESC, city LIMIT 5
tasks.hint: ORDER BY two columns, then LIMIT 5.
tasks.starter:
-- Top cities by customers
SELECT *
FROM customers
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Priciest products
tasks.question: Show the 5 products with the highest list price. Return product_name and list_price, highest first; break ties by product_name A to Z.
tasks.solution: SELECT product_name, list_price FROM products ORDER BY list_price DESC, product_name LIMIT 5
tasks.hint: Sort descending by list_price.
tasks.starter:
-- Priciest products
SELECT *
FROM products
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Delivered revenue by month
tasks.question: For Delivered orders only, what is revenue per month? Return month as YYYY-MM and revenue (2 decimals).
tasks.solution:
SELECT strftime(o.order_date, '%Y-%m') AS month, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)), 2) AS revenue
FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.status = 'Delivered'
GROUP BY 1
tasks.hint: Join orders to order_items. strftime(order_date, '%Y-%m') gives the month.
tasks.starter:
-- Delivered revenue by month
SELECT *
FROM orders
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Average order value by channel
tasks.question: For Delivered orders, what is the average order value (total revenue / number of orders) for App and Web? Return channel and aov (2 decimals).
tasks.solution:
SELECT o.channel, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id), 2) AS aov
FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.status = 'Delivered'
GROUP BY o.channel
tasks.hint: Divide by COUNT(DISTINCT order_id), not COUNT(*): an order can have several lines.
tasks.starter:
-- Average order value by channel
SELECT *
FROM orders
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Category revenue share
tasks.question: For Delivered orders, return each category with its revenue and its share of total revenue in percent. Columns: category, revenue, share_pct (both 2 decimals).
tasks.solution:
SELECT p.category, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)), 2) AS revenue,
       ROUND(100 * SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) / SUM(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount))) OVER (), 2) AS share_pct
FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
WHERE o.status = 'Delivered'
GROUP BY p.category
tasks.hint: SUM(SUM(x)) OVER () gives the grand total next to each group.
tasks.starter:
-- Category revenue share
SELECT *
FROM products
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Top 10 customers
tasks.question: The CRM team wants the 10 customers with the most Delivered revenue. Return customer_id, customer_name, city, revenue (2 decimals), highest first; ties by customer_id.
tasks.solution:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name, c.city, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)), 2) AS revenue
FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.status = 'Delivered'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
ORDER BY revenue DESC, c.customer_id
LIMIT 10
tasks.hint: Three-table join, group by the customer columns, order and limit.
tasks.starter:
-- Top 10 customers
SELECT *
FROM customers
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Repeat purchase rate
tasks.question: Of customers with at least one Delivered order, what percent have 2 or more Delivered orders? Return one value: repeat_rate_pct (2 decimals).
tasks.solution:
WITH c AS (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders WHERE status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY customer_id)
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE n >= 2) / COUNT(*), 2) AS repeat_rate_pct FROM c
tasks.hint: Count orders per customer in a CTE first, then compute the share.
tasks.starter:
-- Repeat purchase rate
SELECT *
FROM orders
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Month-over-month growth
tasks.question: For Delivered revenue by month, return month (YYYY-MM), revenue, prev_revenue and growth_pct (percent change vs previous month, 2 decimals). Sort by month; the first month has empty prev_revenue and growth_pct.
tasks.solution:
WITH m AS (
  SELECT strftime(o.order_date, '%Y-%m') AS month, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) AS revenue
  FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE o.status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY 1)
SELECT month, ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue, ROUND(LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS prev_revenue,
       ROUND(100 * (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month)) / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS growth_pct
FROM m ORDER BY month
tasks.hint: LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) gives the previous month.
tasks.starter:
-- Month-over-month growth
SELECT *
FROM orders
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Best seller in each category
tasks.question: For each category, find the product with the most units sold in Delivered orders (ties go to the lower product_id). Return category, product_name, units.
tasks.solution:
WITH u AS (
  SELECT p.category, p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units
  FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
  WHERE o.status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY 1, 2, 3)
SELECT category, product_name, units FROM (
  SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY units DESC, product_id) AS rn FROM u)
WHERE rn = 1
tasks.hint: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY units DESC, product_id), keep rn = 1.
tasks.starter:
-- Best seller in each category
SELECT *
FROM products
LIMIT 10;

tasks.title: Weekend vs weekday
tasks.question: Split Delivered revenue into Weekend (Saturday, Sunday) and Weekday. result: day_type and revenue (2 decimals).
tasks.solution:
m = order_items.merge(orders, on='order_id')
m = m[m.status == 'Delivered']
m['revenue'] = m.quantity * m.unit_price * (1 - m.discount)
wk = pd.to_datetime(m['order_date']).dt.dayofweek >= 5
m['day_type'] = np.where(wk, 'Weekend', 'Weekday')
result = m.groupby('day_type')['revenue'].sum().round(2)
tasks.hint: .dt.dayofweek is 5 for Saturday and 6 for Sunday.

tasks.title: Cohort repeaters
tasks.question: Group customers by the month of their first Delivered order (cohort, YYYY-MM). For each cohort return customers (how many) and repeaters (how many placed at least one more Delivered order later).
tasks.solution:
d = orders[orders.status == 'Delivered'].copy()
d['order_date'] = pd.to_datetime(d['order_date'])
first = d.groupby('customer_id')['order_date'].min().rename('first')
d = d.join(first, on='customer_id')
c = d.groupby('customer_id').agg(first=('first', 'min'), n=('order_id', 'count'))
c['cohort'] = c['first'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m')
result = c.groupby('cohort').agg(customers=('n', 'size'), repeaters=('n', lambda s: (s >= 2).sum()))
tasks.hint: Find each customer's first order date, then count customers with 2+ orders per cohort.

tasks.title: RFM segments
tasks.question: Using Delivered orders: recency = days from the customer's last order to 2024-12-31, frequency = number of orders. Label Champion if frequency >= 3 and recency <= 60, At risk if recency > 120, otherwise Regular. result: segment and customers.
tasks.solution:
d = orders[orders.status == 'Delivered'].copy()
d['order_date'] = pd.to_datetime(d['order_date'])
g = d.groupby('customer_id').agg(last=('order_date', 'max'), frequency=('order_id', 'count'))
g['recency'] = (pd.Timestamp('2024-12-31') - g['last']).dt.days
g['segment'] = np.select([(g.frequency >= 3) & (g.recency <= 60), g.recency > 120], ['Champion', 'At risk'], 'Regular')
result = g['segment'].value_counts()
tasks.hint: np.select takes a list of conditions and a list of labels, checked in order.
tasks.starter:

tasks.title: Count orders by status
tasks.question: Open the orders sheet. Using COUNTIF, how many orders are Delivered, Cancelled and Returned?
tasks.solution: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'Delivered') AS delivered, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'Cancelled') AS cancelled, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'Returned') AS returned FROM orders
tasks.hint: =COUNTIF(orders!E:E, "Delivered") and the same for the other two.
tasks.explain: Use =COUNTIF(range, "Delivered") on the status column. The three counts add up to the 2,500 orders.

tasks.title: Average list price by category
tasks.question: On the products sheet, use AVERAGEIF to find the average list_price of Kitchen products and of Electronics products (2 decimals).
tasks.solution: SELECT ROUND(AVG(list_price) FILTER (WHERE category = 'Kitchen'), 2) AS kitchen, ROUND(AVG(list_price) FILTER (WHERE category = 'Electronics'), 2) AS electronics FROM products
tasks.hint: =AVERAGEIF(category_range, "Kitchen", list_price_range)
tasks.explain: AVERAGEIF(range, criteria, average_range). Round with =ROUND(x, 2) or by formatting.

tasks.title: Line revenue column
tasks.question: On order_items, add a column revenue = quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount). What is the total of that column, and the largest single line (2 decimals)?
tasks.solution: SELECT ROUND(SUM(quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount)), 2) AS total_revenue, ROUND(MAX(quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount)), 2) AS largest_line FROM order_items
tasks.hint: In F2: =C2*D2*(1-E2), fill down, then SUM and MAX.
tasks.explain: A helper column with =C2*D2*(1-E2), filled down, then =SUM(F:F) and =MAX(F:F). This total includes all statuses.

tasks.title: Look up the channel
tasks.question: Bring the channel of each order into order_items with XLOOKUP (or VLOOKUP) on order_id. How many units (quantity) were sold through App and through Web?
tasks.solution: SELECT SUM(oi.quantity) FILTER (WHERE o.channel = 'App') AS app_units, SUM(oi.quantity) FILTER (WHERE o.channel = 'Web') AS web_units FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o USING (order_id)
tasks.hint: =XLOOKUP(A2, orders!A:A, orders!D:D), then SUMIF on the new column.
tasks.explain: Add a channel column with =XLOOKUP(A2, orders!A:A, orders!D:D), then =SUMIF(channel_col, "App", quantity_col).

tasks.title: Pivot: best category
tasks.question: Build a PivotTable of Delivered revenue by category (you will need status and category on order_items first). Which category has the highest revenue, and how much (2 decimals)?
tasks.solution: SELECT category AS top_category, revenue FROM (SELECT p.category, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)), 2) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o USING (order_id) JOIN products p USING (product_id) WHERE o.status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 1)
tasks.hint: Look up status from orders and category from products, then Insert > PivotTable with a status filter.
tasks.explain: Helper columns: status (XLOOKUP on order_id), category (XLOOKUP on product_id), revenue. PivotTable: Rows = category, Values = Sum of revenue, Filter = status = Delivered. Sort descending.

tasks.title: Revenue by month
tasks.question: Using a PivotTable grouped by month (or SUMIFS with dates), what was Delivered revenue in June 2024 and in December 2024 (2 decimals)?
tasks.solution: SELECT ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) FILTER (WHERE strftime(o.order_date, '%Y-%m') = '2024-06'), 2) AS june, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) FILTER (WHERE strftime(o.order_date, '%Y-%m') = '2024-12'), 2) AS december FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o USING (order_id) WHERE o.status = 'Delivered'
tasks.hint: Add order_date to order_items, then group the date field by Months in the PivotTable.
tasks.explain: Look up order_date and status into order_items. In a PivotTable put order_date in Rows and Group by Months (and Years), Values = Sum of revenue, Filter status = Delivered.

tasks.title: Gross margin
tasks.question: For Delivered order lines, margin = revenue - quantity * cost_price. What is the total margin, and margin as a percent of revenue (2 decimals)?
tasks.solution: SELECT ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount) - oi.quantity * p.cost_price), 2) AS total_margin, ROUND(100 * SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount) - oi.quantity * p.cost_price) / SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)), 2) AS margin_pct FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o USING (order_id) JOIN products p USING (product_id) WHERE o.status = 'Delivered'
tasks.hint: Look up cost_price from products. Margin % = total margin / total revenue * 100.
tasks.explain: Helper columns: status, cost_price (XLOOKUP on product_id), revenue, margin = revenue - quantity*cost_price. Then SUMIFS on status = Delivered for both, and divide.

tasks.title: COUNTIFS on customers
tasks.question: On the customers sheet, use COUNTIFS: how many Business customers are in Maharashtra, and how many Consumer customers signed up in 2024?
tasks.solution: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE segment = 'Business' AND state = 'Maharashtra') AS business_maharashtra, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE segment = 'Consumer' AND year(signup_date) = 2024) AS consumer_2024 FROM customers
tasks.hint: Dates: COUNTIFS(..., signup_date, ">="&DATE(2024,1,1), signup_date, "<="&DATE(2024,12,31)).

tasks.question: Load the four CSV files into Power BI Desktop and build a star schema: order_items to orders (order_id), order_items to products (product_id), orders to customers (customer_id). Then add card visuals: how many orders are there, and how many distinct customers placed an order?
tasks.solution: SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customers_who_ordered FROM orders
tasks.hint: Get Data > Text/CSV for each file, then Model view to check the relationships are one-to-many.

tasks.title: Your first DAX measure
tasks.question: Create Revenue = SUMX(order_items, order_items[quantity] * order_items[unit_price] * (1 - order_items[discount])) and Delivered Revenue = CALCULATE([Revenue], orders[status] = "Delivered"). What do the two cards show (2 decimals)?
tasks.solution: SELECT ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)), 2) AS revenue, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) FILTER (WHERE o.status = 'Delivered'), 2) AS delivered_revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o USING (order_id)
tasks.hint: SUMX iterates row by row; CALCULATE changes the filter.
tasks.explain: Revenue = SUMX(order_items, order_items[quantity] * order_items[unit_price] * (1 - order_items[discount])). Delivered Revenue = CALCULATE([Revenue], orders[status] = "Delivered"). The filter flows from orders to order_items through the relationship.
checklist: Measures live in a measure table or on order_items

tasks.title: Average order value
tasks.question: Create Delivered Orders = CALCULATE(DISTINCTCOUNT(orders[order_id]), orders[status] = "Delivered") and AOV = DIVIDE([Delivered Revenue], [Delivered Orders]). What are Delivered Orders and AOV (2 decimals)?
tasks.solution: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS delivered_orders, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id), 2) AS aov FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o USING (order_id) WHERE o.status = 'Delivered'
tasks.hint: Use DIVIDE instead of / so blanks do not error.
tasks.explain: DIVIDE([Delivered Revenue], [Delivered Orders]) handles divide-by-zero. Only orders with at least one line count, which is all of them here.

tasks.title: Slice it
tasks.question: Add slicers for channel and customer state. With channel = Web and state = Karnataka selected, what is Delivered Revenue (2 decimals), and how many Delivered orders is that?
tasks.solution: SELECT ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)), 2) AS delivered_revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS delivered_orders FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o USING (order_id) JOIN customers c USING (customer_id) WHERE o.status = 'Delivered' AND o.channel = 'Web' AND c.state = 'Karnataka'
tasks.hint: The state slicer comes from customers; it filters orders through the relationship.
tasks.explain: Slicer on orders[channel] and customers[state]. Filters flow customers to orders to order_items, so both measures respond.

tasks.title: Quarter on quarter
tasks.question: Add a date table (CALENDAR from 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31) related to orders[order_date]. What was Delivered Revenue in Q3 and Q4 2024, and Q4 growth vs Q3 in percent (2 decimals)?
tasks.solution:
WITH q AS (SELECT quarter(o.order_date) AS qn, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)) AS r FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o USING (order_id) WHERE o.status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY 1)
SELECT ROUND(MAX(r) FILTER (WHERE qn = 3), 2) AS q3, ROUND(MAX(r) FILTER (WHERE qn = 4), 2) AS q4, ROUND(100 * (MAX(r) FILTER (WHERE qn = 4) / MAX(r) FILTER (WHERE qn = 3) - 1), 2) AS growth_pct FROM q
tasks.hint: Mark the date table as a date table, then use a matrix with Quarter on rows.
tasks.explain: Dates = CALENDAR(DATE(2024,1,1), DATE(2024,12,31)) with Quarter = "Q" & QUARTER([Date]). Growth % = DIVIDE([Q4] - [Q3], [Q3]) * 100, or use a QoQ measure with DATEADD(Dates[Date], -1, QUARTER).
checklist: Date table marked as date table

tasks.title: Build the sales dashboard
tasks.question: Build a one-page dashboard for the category head: KPI cards, revenue by month, revenue by category, a city map or bar chart, and slicers. From your report: which city has the highest Delivered Revenue, and how much (2 decimals)?
tasks.solution: SELECT city AS top_city, revenue FROM (SELECT c.city, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount)), 2) AS revenue FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o USING (order_id) JOIN customers c USING (customer_id) WHERE o.status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 1)
tasks.hint: Use the customer city, not the order city, so it matches the customers table.
tasks.explain: A bar chart of Delivered Revenue by customers[city], sorted descending, gives the answer. A good dashboard: 3 to 4 KPI cards on top, trend line, category bar, city bar, slicers for channel, segment and month.
checklist: KPI cards: Delivered Revenue, Delivered Orders, AOV, Margin %
Line chart of revenue by month
Consistent colours and number formats, a clear title
Exported as PDF or published, ready for your portfolio
